chunks: Besides, if the Imam bears the Divine duty of establishing order and carries the burden of Imamate,
how is it possible for him to be non-existent? Would any sane person see it fair to commission someone non-existent with acts and duties?
Bear in mind that these duties of his are not stipulated to our empowerment of him at all,
but rather, our obligation of empowering and strengthening him is secondary to him carrying out these duties, as explained before and as is very much clear.
ai.seo_question: Why must the Imam exist to bear the burden of Imamate according to Shia theology?
ai.summary: Al-Tusi employs rational logic (aql) to refute the possibility of a 'non-existent' Imam bearing divine duty, arguing that taklif presupposes the actual existence of the agent. He clarifies the causal direction: the community's obligation to empower the Imam is a consequence of his inherent capacity to lead, not the cause of his authority. This establishes the Imamate as an objective reality required for the validity of divine command.
